scenarios.request: Adapt an existing stdio MCP keyword analyser to Fabric.
expected: selects mcp because Fabric owns the task loop
pins MCP revision 2026-07-28
preserves stdio as the connection mode
does not call the provider an autonomous peer
leaves live negotiation and semantic admission NOT VERIFIED

scenarios.request: Adapt an HTTP research service that starts jobs, streams progress, returns artifacts, and supports cancellation.
expected: selects a2a because the remote service owns the task lifecycle
pins A2A version 1.0
requires an Agent Card and task/cancel mapping
uses bounded non-publishing probes

scenarios.request: Make an installed coding CLI available to one Fabric project.
expected: selects local-runner
pins fabric-local-runner/0.1
uses executableRef rather than credentials or an ambient shell command
requires typed input, result, cancellation, and heartbeat behaviour

scenarios.request: Connect a competitor dashboard that only exposes a browser UI.

scenarios.request: Scaffold Fabric files in a repository that already has fabric-agent.json.
expected: refuses to overwrite by default
lists the conflicting path

scenarios.trap: an installer wrote the agent's API key into the entry's env and reused an id that another service already had
scenarios.request: Our example-agent runs as `example-agent mcp` over stdio. Make Fabric find it.
expected: writes a fabric-provider/0.1 entry with fabric_provider.py write, argv as an array, never a shell string
puts env values as secret-ref:<name> references, never the key itself
refuses an id that is already a service (FAC-SEM-013) and says so
points manifest at the agent's fabric-agent.json and removes the entry on uninstall
writes providerId equal to the manifest's provider.id, and refuses the entry when the manifest does not resolve or names another provider (FAC-SEM-014)
